downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.detail: PRs #14095, #14348, #14424 and #14367 added the IIM42653, ICM45605/ICM45686, IIM42652 and ICM40609D drivers after 4.5.5.
downgrade:acc-hardware-new-sensors-reset.note: 4.5.5 doesn't support this accelerometer/gyro chip, so the setting goes back to `set acc_hardware = AUTO`. If your flight controller uses this chip, 4.5.5 may not detect it at all; check that the gyro and accelerometer work before you fly.

downgrade:advanced-tpa-curve-not-in-4-5.detail: PR #13805 added the hyperbolic PID multiplier curve (tpa_curve_type with CLASSIC or HYPERBOLIC, default CLASSIC) as a new feature for wings. 4.5.5 has no equivalent settings.
downgrade:advanced-tpa-curve-not-in-4-5.note: If you had switched to the hyperbolic TPA curve, that curve is gone in 4.5.5 and PID attenuation with throttle will behave differently. Nothing carries over, so check how the quad or wing flies and retune TPA if needed.

downgrade:altitude-hold-settings-not-in-.detail: These settings come from the altitude hold and autopilot work (for example PRs #13816, #13884 and #13975), with names later made consistent by PR #14136. They don't exist in 4.5.5.
downgrade:altitude-hold-settings-not-in-.note: Altitude hold doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so this tuning has no equivalent there.

downgrade:autopilot-pid-settings-not-in-.detail: PR #13975 and PR #14136 introduced and renamed the autopilot settings in 2025.12.5. 4.5.5 has no counterparts for these ones.
downgrade:autopilot-pid-settings-not-in-.note: Altitude and position hold don't exist in 4.5.5, so these values have no equivalent there. Keep a copy of your 2025.12.5 settings if you plan to go back.

downgrade:blackbox-virtual-device-reset.detail: PR #14325 added the VIRTUAL blackbox device for SITL; 4.5.5 only knows NONE, SPIFLASH, SDCARD and SERIAL.
downgrade:blackbox-virtual-device-reset.note: The VIRTUAL blackbox device only exists in the simulator (SITL) build and not in 4.5.5, so blackbox logging is off (`set blackbox_device = NONE`). To log on real hardware, pick SPIFLASH, SDCARD or SERIAL, e.g. `set blackbox_device = SPIFLASH`.

downgrade:crash-dthreshold-scale-changed.detail: PR #13803 multiplies the gyro-delta threshold by 1000 internally but kept the 10..2000 range and the default of 50. That means no value in one version matches a value in the other.
downgrade:crash-dthreshold-scale-changed.note: 2025.12.5 and 4.5.5 read this number on scales 1000x apart, so your value would behave very differently in 4.5.5. The 4.5.5 default of 50 is used instead. If you had tuned crash detection, pick a new value for 4.5.5 and test it, e.g. `set crash_dthreshold = 50`.

downgrade:crashflip-auto-rearm-new.detail: PR #14734 added an explicit auto-rearm control to the crashflip settings. Before that, auto-rearm was not a separate setting.
downgrade:crashflip-auto-rearm-new.note: 4.5.5 has no separate setting for crashflip auto-rearm, so there is nothing to set again there. Check how crashflip re-arming behaves on your quad after flashing.

downgrade:crashflip-rate-replaces-expo.detail: PR #13905 replaced the stick expo setting with a rotation-rate limit that has attitude attenuation, so the two settings have no direct equivalent.
downgrade:crashflip-rate-replaces-expo.note: Your crashflip rate value can't be carried over, because 4.5.5 uses `crashflip_expo` instead, and it means something different. 4.5.5 will use its own default for `crashflip_expo`. If you want a different crashflip feel, set `crashflip_expo` yourself in the CLI.

downgrade:d-gets-peak-from-d-max.detail: PR #13908 made the D gain the base and d_max_roll/d_max_pitch/d_max_yaw the peak, where 4.5.5 uses the D gain as the peak. PR #13933 made dynamic D active only when D is above 0 and the max D is above D, so the converter uses the same condition.
downgrade:d-gets-peak-from-d-max.note: In 4.5.5 the D gain is the peak of dynamic D, not the base. If dynamic D was active in 2025.12.5, meaning the D gain was above 0 and the max D above it, the max D value becomes this D gain. Otherwise your D value carries over unchanged.

downgrade:d-max-advance-reset.detail: PR #14629 made D-max advance independent of the gain in 2025.12.5; in 4.5.5 the setpoint boost is d_max_gain x advance / 100, so the same number acts differently.
downgrade:d-max-advance-reset.note: In 2025.12.5 D-max advance works on its own, but in 4.5.5 its effect is scaled by d_max_gain, so the same number can act differently. The 4.5.5 default of 20 is used. If you had changed it, retune it after flashing 4.5.5.

downgrade:d-max-folded-back-into-d-and-d.detail: PR #13908 swapped the dynamic D model: in 2025.12.5 d_roll is the base D and d_max_roll the peak, while in 4.5.5 d_roll is the peak and d_min_roll the floor.
downgrade:d-max-folded-back-into-d-and-d.note: Your D range is converted to 4.5.5's layout: the peak D goes into d_roll, d_pitch and d_yaw, and your base D goes into d_min_roll, d_min_pitch and d_min_yaw as the lower floor. If the base D was 0 or the peak was not above it, dynamic D is turned off (d_min_roll, d_min_pitch and d_min_yaw are set to 0). Check your D values after loading.

downgrade:d-min-rebuilt-from-base-d.detail: PR #13908 swapped the roles. In 4.5.5 the D gain is the peak and d_min_roll/d_min_pitch/d_min_yaw are the base. In 2025.12.5 the D gain is the base and d_max_roll/d_max_pitch/d_max_yaw are the peak.
downgrade:d-min-rebuilt-from-base-d.note: In 4.5.5 these settings hold the lower (base) D of dynamic D. If dynamic D was active in 2025.12.5, meaning the D gain was above 0 and the max D above it, your 2025.12.5 D gain becomes this value. Otherwise it is set to 0, which turns dynamic D off. Check your D tune after converting.

downgrade:debug-mode-new-modes-reset.note: This debug mode doesn't exist in 4.5.5 and has no equivalent there, so the board's default debug mode is used. It only affects what blackbox logs record. If you need a debug mode, pick one that 4.5.5 offers.

downgrade:debug-mode-values-renamed-or-r.detail: PR #14533 renamed the DUAL_GYRO_* debug modes to MULTI_GYRO_*, PR #13908 renamed D_MIN to D_MAX, and PR #13954 renamed GPS_RESCUE_THROTTLE_PID to AUTOPILOT_ALTITUDE. Each pair logs the same thing, so the old names are used again.
downgrade:debug-mode-values-renamed-or-r.note: Your debug mode was changed back to its older name in 4.5.5, for example MULTI_GYRO_RAW becomes DUAL_GYRO_RAW and D_MAX becomes D_MIN. It logs the same data, so you don't need to do anything. The debug mode only affects what goes into Blackbox logs.

downgrade:dshot-edt-force-reset.detail: PR #14532 added FORCE, which also makes the firmware always decode extended telemetry. 4.5.5 only has OFF and ON, and it has no always-decode mode.
downgrade:dshot-edt-force-reset.note: 4.5.5 has no FORCE option for extended DShot telemetry, so the 4.5.5 default of OFF is used. If you want extended DShot telemetry in 4.5.5, use `set dshot_edt = ON`.

downgrade:dshot-idle-value-from-motor-id.detail: PR #13936 renamed dshot_idle_value to motor_idle and kept the same 0-2000 range and DShot calculation (value × 0.01 percent).
downgrade:dshot-idle-value-from-motor-id.note: Your motor idle value was copied to the older setting name. Both use the same units, so motors idle the same way and you don't need to do anything.

downgrade:dyn-notch-count-clamped-to-5.detail: PR #13750 raised the maximum dynamic notch count from 5 to 7. 4.5.5 still has the old 0-5 range.
downgrade:dyn-notch-count-clamped-to-5.note: 4.5.5 allows at most 5 dynamic notches. A count of 6 or 7 was lowered to 5, and smaller counts carry over unchanged.

downgrade:failsafe-landing-time-renamed-.detail: PR #13816 replaced failsafe_off_delay (0.1 s units, 0-200) with failsafe_landing_time (seconds, 0-250).
downgrade:failsafe-landing-time-renamed-.note: 4.5.5 stores this landing timeout under the older name failsafe_off_delay, counted in tenths of a second. Your value was multiplied by 10 and capped at 200 (20 seconds), so any timeout longer than 20 seconds is now 20 seconds.

downgrade:failsafe-off-delay-from-landin.detail: PR #13816 renamed failsafe_off_delay (0.1 s units, max 200) to failsafe_landing_time (seconds, max 250). The downgrade multiplies by 10 and caps the result.
downgrade:failsafe-off-delay-from-landin.note: This failsafe landing timeout comes from your failsafe_landing_time value, converted from seconds to tenths of a second. It is capped at 200 (20 seconds), so any longer timeout is now 20 seconds.

downgrade:feedforward-boost-reset.detail: PR #13576 reworked feedforward for 4.6. It changed the internal boost multiplier from 0.1x to 0.001x the setting and replaced the yaw boost with a yaw-hold component. The range (0-50) and default (15) stayed the same.
downgrade:feedforward-boost-reset.note: Feedforward boost is now at the 4.5.5 default of 15. The two versions use this value differently, so your old number might not give the same feel. Test fly, and if you want more or less boost, retune it with e.g. `set feedforward_boost = 15`.

downgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-rese.detail: PR #13576 reworked the jitter-reduction logic so feedforward is no longer forced abruptly to zero. It also changed the internal inverse factor from 1/(2*v) to 1/(1+v). The range (0-20) and default (7) stayed the same.
downgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-rese.note: Feedforward jitter reduction is now at the 4.5.5 default of 7. 4.5.5 uses this number in a different formula, so your old value might not give the same jitter attenuation. Test fly and retune if needed, e.g. `set feedforward_jitter_factor = 7`.

downgrade:feedforward-smooth-factor-rate.detail: PR #14411 changed the smoothing from a per-packet factor (strength depends on packet rate) to a time constant fixed at 250 Hz. It also raised the default from 25 to 65 and merged the feedforward cutoff into the setpoint cutoff.
downgrade:feedforward-smooth-factor-rate.note: Feedforward smoothing is now at the 4.5.5 default of 25. In 4.5.5, how strong a given value smooths depends on your radio link's packet rate. Your old value was tuned for a fixed 250 Hz basis, so it can't be converted exactly. Retune if needed, e.g. `set feedforward_smooth_factor = 25`.

downgrade:gps-provider-virtual-reset.detail: PR #14131 added the VIRTUAL GPS provider for simulator (SITL) builds. The NMEA, UBLOX and MSP values are the same in both versions.
downgrade:gps-provider-virtual-reset.note: 4.5.5 has no virtual (simulated) GPS provider, so the board's default provider applies. If you fly a real GPS, set its protocol, e.g. `set gps_provider = UBLOX`, or NMEA or MSP.

downgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-clamped.detail: PR #13816 replaced gps_rescue_landing_alt (1-15 m) with a shared landing altitude setting that allows 0-200 m. The older firmware can't hold values outside its smaller range.
downgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-clamped.note: Your landing altitude goes back into gps_rescue_landing_alt, which only accepts 1 to 15 metres. A value of 0 becomes 1, and anything above 15 becomes 15. If your value was outside that range, check that the result suits you, e.g. `set gps_rescue_landing_alt = 4`.

downgrade:gyro-enabled-bitmask-removed.detail: PR #14383 replaced the three-way gyro_to_use selector with gyro_enabled_bitmask to support more than two gyros. In the bitmask, bit 0 is gyro 1 and bit 1 is gyro 2.
downgrade:gyro-enabled-bitmask-removed.note: 4.5.5 chooses gyros with gyro_to_use (FIRST, SECOND or BOTH) instead of a bitmask. Your bitmask was turned into gyro_to_use using its gyro 1 and gyro 2 bits only. If the mask enabled no gyro, or only gyros 3 and up, you get FIRST, so check that the right gyro is active after loading.

downgrade:gyro-to-use-from-enabled-bitma.detail: PR #14383 replaced the three-way gyro_to_use selector with gyro_enabled_bitmask plus per-gyro gyro_N_enabled settings. In the bitmask, bit 0 is gyro 1 and bit 1 is gyro 2.
downgrade:gyro-to-use-from-enabled-bitma.note: 4.5.5 chooses gyros with gyro_to_use (FIRST, SECOND or BOTH) instead of a bitmask. Your bitmask was turned into gyro_to_use using its gyro 1 and gyro 2 bits only. If the mask enabled no gyro, or only gyros 3 and up, you get FIRST, so check that the right gyro is active after loading.

downgrade:hse-26mhz-reset.detail: PR #14261 added 26 MHz support for STM32G4 only in 2025.12. Before that, the G4 clock setup returned early for 26 and ignored it.
downgrade:hse-26mhz-reset.note: 4.5.5 can't use a 26 MHz external crystal on STM32G4 boards and silently ignores that value. The board's own 4.5.5 default is used instead. If your board isn't STM32G4 and really needs 26 MHz, put it back with `set system_hse_mhz = 26`.

downgrade:iterm-windup-meaning-changed.detail: PR #13543 replaced the motor-saturation windup point with a per-axis cap: iTerm is limited to iterm_windup percent of the axis's PID sum limit. The same PR changed the minimum from 30 to 20 and the default from 85 to 80.
downgrade:iterm-windup-meaning-changed.note: This number controls something different in 4.5.5, so your value can't be carried over and the 4.5.5 default of 85 is used instead. In 4.5.5 it is the motor-mix saturation point above which iTerm growth slows on all axes. In 2025.12.5 it is a per-axis iTerm cap. Keep 85 unless you have a reason to tune it again (the 4.5.5 range is 30-100).

downgrade:mag-bustype-new-values-reset.detail: In 2025.12 a new QSPI bus type was added without updating the bus name list. From SLAVE onward, each name stores the next bus type: SLAVE stores QSPI, which has no compass driver, and GYROAUTO stores the gyro-slave bus that 4.5.5 calls SLAVE.
downgrade:mag-bustype-new-values-reset.note: In 2025.12.5 this compass bus name stored a different bus than the same name selects in 4.5.5, so it can't be carried over safely. Your board's default compass bus applies. If your compass is connected through the gyro, use `set mag_bustype = SLAVE` and check that the compass is detected.

downgrade:mag-declination-wrapped-to-pos.detail: PR #14019 and PR #14206 changed the setting to a signed range of -300 to 300. Older firmware expected the 0 to 3599 wrapped form.
downgrade:mag-declination-wrapped-to-pos.note: 4.5.5 stores declination as 0 to 3599 tenths of a degree, so a west (negative) declination is written as 3600 plus the value, for example -50 becomes 3550. Your heading correction stays the same.

downgrade:min-throttle-rebuilt-from-moto.detail: PR #13936 removed min_throttle and made the analog idle output min_command + motor_idle × 0.1. The downgrade rebuilds min_throttle with the same formula.
downgrade:min-throttle-rebuilt-from-moto.note: 4.5.5 sets the analog-ESC idle output with min_throttle. It was calculated from your min_command and motor_idle as min_command + motor_idle/10, the same idle level your newer firmware used. It is clamped to 750-2250.

downgrade:mixer-octox8p-not-nameable.detail: PR #14418 added OCTOX8P to the CLI's list of mixer names in 2025.12. 4.5.5 already had the same OctoX8P motor layout inside the firmware, but its CLI has no name to select it.
downgrade:mixer-octox8p-not-nameable.note: The 4.5.5 CLI can't select the OctoX8P mixer by name, so your board's default mixer applies. Set up your octocopter's motor mix again in 4.5.5, and check the motor order and spin direction before arming.

downgrade:opticalflow-feature-absent.detail: Optical flow support came with PR #14038, which is not in 4.5.5.
downgrade:opticalflow-feature-absent.note: 4.5.5 has no optical flow feature, so an optical flow sensor won't be used after the downgrade. Nothing needs to be set; just don't count on that sensor in 4.5.5.

downgrade:pinio-box-unsupported-modes-cl.detail: PR #13816 and PR #13975 reused mode IDs 3 and 11 for ALTHOLD and POS HOLD, and PR #13105 added ID 55 for CHIRP. 4.5.5 has no mode with these IDs.
downgrade:pinio-box-unsupported-modes-cl.note: Any PINIO pin assigned to ALTHOLD, POS HOLD or CHIRP was set to 255 (no mode), because 4.5.5 doesn't have those modes. A pin left on them would never switch. All other assignments carry over unchanged. If you want such a pin driven by a different mode, set its pinio_box entry again in the CLI.

downgrade:position-hold-settings-not-in-.detail: PR #13975 added the position hold settings in 2025.12.5, and PR #14069 updated related defines. 4.5.5 has no counterparts.
downgrade:position-hold-settings-not-in-.note: Position hold doesn't exist in 4.5.5, so these values have no equivalent there. Keep a copy of your 2025.12.5 settings if you plan to go back.

downgrade:prearm-allow-rearm-not-in-4-5.detail: PR #14013 added the option to re-arm without resetting the prearm switch. 4.5.5 has no setting for it.
downgrade:prearm-allow-rearm-not-in-4-5.note: If you had this turned on, your re-arm behaviour may differ after the downgrade, so test arming on the bench with props off before flying.

downgrade:rangefinder-new-hardware-reset.detail: PR #13980 added the MTF01, MTF02, MTF01P and MTF02P rangefinders and PR #14376 added TFNOVA. Both appended them to the end of the list, so they have no equivalent in 4.5.5.
downgrade:rangefinder-new-hardware-reset.note: 4.5.5 doesn't support this rangefinder model, so the rangefinder is turned off (NONE). 4.5.5 only knows HCSR04, TFMINI and TF02. If you use one of those, set it with e.g. `set rangefinder_hardware = TFMINI`.

downgrade:rc-ff-cutoff-from-setpoint-cut.detail: PR #14411 merged the feedforward smoothing cutoff into rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff, so newer firmware always uses one cutoff for both. Setting the old separate value equal to the setpoint cutoff gives the same behaviour.
downgrade:rc-ff-cutoff-from-setpoint-cut.note: 4.5.5 has a separate cutoff for feedforward smoothing. It is given the same value as your rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff, so feedforward is filtered the same way as in 2025.12.5. You don't need to do anything.

downgrade:rescue-hover-throttle-from-ap-.detail: PR #13816 merged the GPS Rescue hover throttle into a shared hover throttle setting, which PR #14136 later named ap_hover_throttle. Every ap_hover_throttle value fits the older 1000-2000 range.
downgrade:rescue-hover-throttle-from-ap-.note: Your GPS Rescue hover throttle comes from your shared ap_hover_throttle value. Both use the same units, so nothing changes and you don't need to do anything.

downgrade:rescue-throttle-min-from-ap-th.detail: PR #13954 moved GPS Rescue onto a shared altitude controller and removed its own throttle minimum. PR #14136 named the shared setting ap_throttle_min.
downgrade:rescue-throttle-min-from-ap-th.note: In 4.5.5, GPS Rescue has its own minimum throttle setting. Your shared autopilot minimum throttle (ap_throttle_min) was copied into it. The units are the same, so nothing needs to change.

downgrade:resource-new-owners-dropped.detail: 2025.12.5 added these three functions you can assign to a pin with the resource command; none were renamed or removed. 4.5.5 rejects lines that name them.
downgrade:resource-new-owners-dropped.note: 4.5.5 doesn't recognise the pin functions GYRO_CLKIN, PIOUART_TX or PIOUART_RX, so these pin assignments can't be set there. Whatever relied on them won't be set up after the downgrade. Check your other resource assignments before flying.

downgrade:serial-port-identifiers-renumb.detail: PR #13585 and PR #14094 renumbered the serial port identifiers and 2025.12.5 prints port names, which 4.5.5 would misread as UART1. PR #14192 and PR #14697 raised the GPS and telemetry baud limits above the 115200 that 4.5.5 accepts.
downgrade:serial-port-identifiers-renumb.note: Port names are converted back to the port numbers 4.5.5 uses (for example UART1 becomes 0, VCP becomes 20), so your port functions stay on the same ports. Ports 4.5.5 doesn't have (UART0, PIOUART) and GPS or telemetry speeds above 115200 can't be carried over; re-create those ports with a speed 4.5.5 supports.

downgrade:serial-port-ids-renumbered.detail: PRs #13585 and #14094 renumbered the serial port identifiers and added UART0; other ports are converted back to 4.5.5 numbers automatically. PR #14192 raised the GPS speed limit to 230400 and PR #14697 raised the telemetry limit to 460800, but 4.5.5 rejects the whole serial line above 115200.
downgrade:serial-port-ids-renumbered.note: This port can't be set up in 4.5.5: either the port (UART0 or a PIOUART) doesn't exist there, or it uses a GPS speed above 115200 or a telemetry speed above 115200, which 4.5.5 rejects. Set the port up again in 4.5.5 on a port it has and at 115200 or lower, and check that the connected device still talks at that speed.

downgrade:serialrx-mavlink-reset.detail: PR #14681 added MAVLINK as a new serial receiver provider at the end of the list. Older firmware has no equivalent.
downgrade:serialrx-mavlink-reset.note: 4.5.5 has no MAVLink receiver protocol, so your board's default serial receiver protocol applies. Your receiver may not work until you pick a protocol that 4.5.5 supports and your receiver can output, e.g. `set serialrx_provider = CRSF`.

downgrade:thr-hover-removed.detail: PR #14229 split the single throttle curve midpoint into thr_mid (stick position) and thr_hover (throttle output at that point). 4.5.5 can only describe a curve where the two are equal.
downgrade:thr-hover-removed.note: 4.5.5 has no separate hover point. Its throttle curve midpoint uses thr_mid as both the stick position and the throttle output, so a hover value different from thr_mid can't be kept there. Your thr_mid carries over unchanged.

downgrade:thr-mid-carries-over.detail: PR #14229 made thr_mid only the stick position (x) of the midpoint and added thr_hover for the output (y). PR #14356 still builds the curve through those two values. 4.5.5 uses one value for both.
downgrade:thr-mid-carries-over.note: The value carries over unchanged. In 4.5.5, thr_mid sets both the stick position of the curve midpoint and the throttle output there. If your thr_hover was different from thr_mid, the throttle curve around mid-stick will feel a little different, so check your hover throttle after flashing.

downgrade:tpa-low-rate-negative-clamped.detail: PR #13661 allowed negative tpa_low_rate values on wing builds, which give more PID at zero throttle. 4.5.5 stores the setting as an unsigned value from 0 to 100.
downgrade:tpa-low-rate-negative-clamped.note: 4.5.5 only accepts 0 to 100 here and can't raise PIDs at low throttle. A negative value becomes 0, which means no low-throttle TPA. Values from 0 to 100 carry over unchanged.

downgrade:tpa-mode-pds-reset.detail: PR #14010 added PDS for wings, which also makes the S-term dynamic with throttle. 4.5.5 only offers PD and D.
downgrade:tpa-mode-pds-reset.note: 4.5.5 has no PDS TPA mode, and nothing there works the same way, so TPA now uses the 4.5.5 default, D. Check how the aircraft flies at high throttle. If you want P attenuated as well, use `set tpa_mode = PD`.

upgrade:angle-limit-max-lowered-to-80.detail: PR #13975 lowered the maximum of angle_limit from 85 to 80. The meaning and units did not change.
upgrade:angle-limit-max-lowered-to-80.note: The highest allowed angle limit is now 80 degrees instead of 85. Values of 80 or less carry over unchanged, and values from 81 to 85 are set to 80. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:ap-hover-throttle-from-rescue-ho.detail: PR #13954 moved the GPS Rescue throttle settings into a shared autopilot configuration, and PR #14136 renamed this one to ap_hover_throttle with a range of 1100-1700. The default stays the same.
upgrade:ap-hover-throttle-from-rescue-ho.note: The GPS Rescue hover throttle is now the shared autopilot hover throttle, ap_hover_throttle. Your value carries over in the same units, but it must now be between 1100 and 1700, so values outside that range are moved to the nearest limit.

upgrade:ap-throttle-max-from-rescue-max.detail: PR #13954 merged the GPS Rescue throttle limits into the shared autopilot altitude control, and PR #14136 renamed this one to ap_throttle_max with a range of 1400-2000.
upgrade:ap-throttle-max-from-rescue-max.note: The GPS Rescue maximum throttle is now the shared autopilot limit, ap_throttle_max, and in 2025.12.5 it also caps altitude hold and position hold. Your value carries over in the same units, but it must now be between 1400 and 2000, so lower values are raised to 1400.

upgrade:ap-throttle-min-from-rescue-min.detail: PR #13954 merged the GPS Rescue throttle limits into the shared autopilot altitude control, and PR #14136 renamed this one to ap_throttle_min with a range of 1050-1400.
upgrade:ap-throttle-min-from-rescue-min.note: The GPS Rescue minimum throttle is now the shared autopilot limit, ap_throttle_min. Your value carries over in the same units, but it must now be between 1050 and 1400, so values outside that range are moved to the nearest limit.

upgrade:crash-dthreshold-scale-changed.detail: PR #13803 fixed a crash-recovery scaling bug by multiplying the internal threshold by 1000. The range (10..2000) and default (50) did not change, so no conversion keeps the old behaviour.
upgrade:crash-dthreshold-scale-changed.note: This threshold now works on a scale 1000x different from before, so your old number would behave very differently. It has been set back to `set crash_dthreshold = 50`. If you rely on crash recovery, re-tune it from there.

upgrade:crashflip-expo-reinterpreted.detail: PR #13905 replaced the crashflip_expo setting (0-100, default 35) with crashflip_rate (0-250 in deg/s*10, default 0) and removed the expo mixer code.
upgrade:crashflip-expo-reinterpreted.note: Crashflip no longer uses a stick expo. It now has a rotation-rate limit with attitude attenuation, so your old expo value doesn't carry over and the new setting starts at its default. If you want to tune it, change `crashflip_rate` (range 0-250).

upgrade:custom-gyro-alignment-removed.detail: PR #14688 removed the gyro_N_align_roll/pitch/yaw settings from the CLI; a smaller alignment adjustment is planned to replace them.
upgrade:custom-gyro-alignment-removed.note: Custom gyro alignment angles can no longer be set. If you used them to correct how the flight controller is mounted, set the same correction with board alignment instead (`set align_board_roll`, `set align_board_pitch`, `set align_board_yaw`, in degrees). Board alignment turns all sensors together, so check the orientation before flying.

upgrade:d-gain-becomes-base-d.detail: PR #13908 made the D gain the base value and moved the peak into a separate setting. PR #13933 made dynamic D run only when the peak is above the base, and PR #13822 moved in-flight D adjustments to the base value.
upgrade:d-gain-becomes-base-d.note: The D gains now hold the base (lowest) D, not the peak. Where dynamic D was active, each axis takes your old dynamic-D floor value and the old peak moves to the new peak-D setting. Where dynamic D was off, the D gain carries over unchanged.

upgrade:d-max-advance-reset.detail: PR #14629 made D-max advance independent of d_max_gain: the setpoint boost used to be d_max_gain x advance / 100 and is now the advance alone. The same PR also moved where the D-max multiplier is applied (before TPA).
upgrade:d-max-advance-reset.note: The D-max advance effect no longer depends on d_max_gain, so your old value may not give the same feel. It has been set back to `set d_max_advance = 20`. If you had tuned it, re-tune it from there.

upgrade:d-max-takes-old-peak-d.detail: PR #13908 reversed the dynamic D model. The D gain used to be the peak, with a separate minimum as the floor. Now the D gain is the base and a separate maximum setting holds the peak; 0 still means off.
upgrade:d-max-takes-old-peak-d.note: Your old peak D (the D gain you had set) now goes into the new peak-D settings, and your old dynamic-D floor becomes the base D gain. If dynamic D was off in your old tune, the peak is set to 0, which means disabled. Your tune should stay the same, so no action is needed.

upgrade:debug-mode-gyro-scaled-removed.detail: PR #13101 removed GYRO_SCALED as obsolete, because the same unfiltered gyro data is already logged. No other debug mode replaces it.
upgrade:debug-mode-gyro-scaled-removed.note: GYRO_SCALED is no longer a debug mode in 2025.12.5, so your board's default debug mode applies instead. If you log blackbox with a debug mode, choose another one, e.g. `set debug_mode = GYRO_RAW`.

upgrade:debug-mode-values-renamed.detail: PR #14533 renamed DUAL_GYRO_RAW, DUAL_GYRO_DIFF and DUAL_GYRO_SCALED to MULTI_GYRO_RAW, MULTI_GYRO_DIFF and MULTI_GYRO_SCALED. PR #13908 renamed D_MIN to D_MAX, and PR #13954 renamed GPS_RESCUE_THROTTLE_PID to AUTOPILOT_ALTITUDE.
upgrade:debug-mode-values-renamed.note: Some debug mode names changed in the new firmware, so the converter switched your value to the new name. The renamed modes log the same data as before, so your blackbox setup works the same way.

upgrade:dyn-idle-start-increase-removed.detail: PR #13906 removed the parameter (default 50) and made the start limit use the static idle value instead, with no replacement setting.
upgrade:dyn-idle-start-increase-removed.note: The initial dynamic idle limit before takeoff is no longer adjustable and your old value is not used. It now follows your static idle value, so check that value if you tuned idle behaviour.

upgrade:failsafe-landing-time-in-seconds.detail: PR #13816 replaced failsafe_off_delay (0.1 s units, 0-200) with failsafe_landing_time (seconds, 0-250).
upgrade:failsafe-landing-time-in-seconds.note: The landing-phase timeout now counts whole seconds, not tenths of a second. Your old failsafe_off_delay value was divided by 10 and rounded, so any fraction of a second is lost. If you want a different time, set it in seconds, e.g. `set failsafe_landing_time = 60`.

upgrade:failsafe-off-delay-renamed.detail: PR #13816 renamed failsafe_off_delay (0.1 s units, max 200) to failsafe_landing_time (seconds, max 250) and changed the timer to match.
upgrade:failsafe-off-delay-renamed.note: This setting is now called failsafe_landing_time and counts whole seconds, not tenths of a second. Your value was divided by 10, rounded and carried over under the new name.

upgrade:feedforward-boost-reset.detail: PR #13576 reworked feedforward: the internal boost multiplier became 100x smaller, and yaw boost was replaced by a yaw-hold component. The range (0-50) and default (15) stayed the same.
upgrade:feedforward-boost-reset.note: Your feedforward boost value was set back to the 2025.12.5 default of 15, because the way boost is calculated changed. If you had tuned it, test-fly and adjust again, e.g. `set feedforward_boost = 15` as a starting point.

upgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-reset.detail: PR #13576 changed the jitter factor formula from 1/(2*v) to 1/(1+v) and reworked jitter reduction so feedforward is no longer forced abruptly to zero. The range (0-20) and default (7) are unchanged.
upgrade:feedforward-jitter-factor-reset.note: Your feedforward jitter factor was set back to the 2025.12.5 default of 7, because the jitter reduction it controls was reworked. If you had tuned it, test-fly and adjust it again, e.g. `set feedforward_jitter_factor = 7`.

upgrade:feedforward-smoothing-fixed-time.detail: PR #14411 changed the smoothing from a per-packet factor, whose strength depended on the link's packet rate, to a time constant fixed to a 250 Hz rate. It also raised the default from 25 to 65 and merged the feedforward cutoff into the setpoint cutoff.
upgrade:feedforward-smoothing-fixed-time.note: Your feedforward smoothing value was set to the new 2025.12.5 default of 65, because the same number now gives different smoothing unless your radio link runs at 250 Hz. If you had tuned it, test-fly and adjust it again with `set feedforward_smooth_factor = <value>` (0-95).

upgrade:ff-smoothing-cutoff-merged.detail: PR #14411 removed the separate feedforward cutoff and merged it into the setpoint cutoff.
upgrade:ff-smoothing-cutoff-merged.note: Feedforward smoothing now always uses the same cutoff as rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff, so a separate feedforward cutoff can't be kept. If you had set a different feedforward value, check that your rc_smoothing_setpoint_cutoff still suits you.

upgrade:gps-rescue-gains-clamped-to-200.detail: PR #13954 lowered the CLI maximum for the GPS Rescue velocity P, I, D and yaw P gains from 255 to 200. Every value allowed in the new version also fits the old range.
upgrade:gps-rescue-gains-clamped-to-200.note: These GPS Rescue gains now go up to 200 instead of 255. Values of 200 or less carry over unchanged. Anything higher was lowered to 200, so if you had set one above 200, test GPS Rescue carefully before relying on it.

upgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-renamed-a.detail: The GPS Rescue landing altitude became a shared autopilot setting, and PR #14136 gave it the ap_ prefix. GPS Rescue still starts its landing phase below this height and uses a landing circle of half this value around home.
upgrade:gps-rescue-landing-alt-renamed-a.note: Your GPS Rescue landing altitude carries over unchanged under the new name ap_landing_altitude_m. It still means the same thing in metres, so you don't need to do anything.

upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-pid-removed.detail: PRs #13816, #13884 and #14108 added altitude hold and shared altitude-control parameters (the ap_* settings) and removed these throttle PID settings.
upgrade:gps-rescue-throttle-pid-removed.note: Your tuned numbers are not carried over. GPS Rescue now shares its altitude control with altitude hold, through `ap_altitude_p`, `ap_altitude_i` and `ap_altitude_d`, so review those if you tuned rescue altitude behaviour. P and D numbers mean roughly the same as before; I is about three times stronger, so divide an old I value by 3 if you want the same effect.

upgrade:gyro-1-enabled-from-gyro-to-use.detail: PR #14383 added gyro_1_enabled as bit 0 of gyro_enabled_bitmask, replacing gyro_to_use. Together with gyro_2_enabled, it keeps the full FIRST/SECOND/BOTH choice.
upgrade:gyro-1-enabled-from-gyro-to-use.note: The single gyro_to_use selector was replaced by separate on/off switches for each gyro. Your choice carries over automatically: the first gyro is ON if gyro_to_use was FIRST or BOTH, and OFF otherwise. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:gyro-2-enabled-from-gyro-to-use.detail: PR #14383 added gyro_2_enabled as bit 1 of gyro_enabled_bitmask, replacing gyro_to_use. Together with gyro_1_enabled, it keeps the full FIRST/SECOND/BOTH choice.
upgrade:gyro-2-enabled-from-gyro-to-use.note: The single gyro_to_use selector was replaced by separate on/off switches for each gyro. Your choice carries over automatically: the second gyro is ON if gyro_to_use was SECOND or BOTH, and OFF otherwise. You don't need to do anything.

upgrade:gyro-enabled-bitmask-from-gyro-t.detail: PR #14383 added support for more than two gyros and replaced gyro_to_use with gyro_enabled_bitmask, where each bit enables one gyro. PR #14684 only corrected the CLI name.
upgrade:gyro-enabled-bitmask-from-gyro-t.note: Your gyro selection now uses a bitmask, and the converter translated it for you: FIRST becomes 1, SECOND becomes 2 and BOTH becomes 3. The same gyros stay enabled, so there is nothing to do.

upgrade:gyro-sensor-align-fixed-by-board.detail: PR #14648 removed the ability to set the gyro alignment at run time, including the CLI entries and the MSP alignment read/write. Board alignment, the board's mounting orientation in the frame, can still be set.
upgrade:gyro-sensor-align-fixed-by-board.note: Gyro alignment now comes from the board's own configuration and can't be changed. To correct how the board is mounted in your frame, use board alignment (`set align_board_roll`, `set align_board_pitch`, `set align_board_yaw`, in degrees). Check the orientation before flying.

upgrade:iterm-limit-derived-from-windup.detail: PR #13543 removed the iterm_limit CLI entry. The I-term limit is now iterm_windup percent of the pidsum limit, applied per axis.
upgrade:iterm-limit-derived-from-windup.note: The I-term limit is no longer a separate setting, so your old value is not carried over. It is now worked out from `iterm_windup` and `pidsum_limit`. The meaning of `iterm_windup` also changed, so check both values rather than reusing old numbers.

upgrade:iterm-windup-now-per-axis-cap.detail: PR #13543 removed the old point of motor saturation above which I-term growth was scaled down on all axes at once. It replaced it with a separate I-term cap for each axis, set as a percentage of that axis's PID sum limit. This takes over from the removed iterm_limit, lowers the minimum from 30 to 20 and changes the default from 85 to 80.
upgrade:iterm-windup-now-per-axis-cap.note: In 2025.12.5 this number controls something different, so your old value would not give the same result. The 2025.12.5 default of 80 is used instead. If you had tuned it, re-tune from there and set your value again, e.g. `set iterm_windup = 80`.

upgrade:legacy-accelerometer-drivers-rem.detail: PR #14087 removed the legacy ADXL345, BMA280, LSM303DLHC and MMA8452 drivers and took them out of the acc_hardware list. They have no equivalent in 2025.12.5.
upgrade:legacy-accelerometer-drivers-rem.note: 2025.12.5 no longer supports this accelerometer, so the setting is now `set acc_hardware = AUTO` and the board will detect a supported sensor on its own. If your board actually uses one of these older sensors, the accelerometer won't work on 2025.12.5.

upgrade:mag-bustype-slave-gyroauto-remov.detail: A new QSPI bus type was added to the firmware's internal list of bus types, but no CLI name was added for it. From 2025.12 on, the names from SLAVE onward store a different value than in 4.5.5. NONE, I2C and SPI are unaffected.
upgrade:mag-bustype-slave-gyroauto-remov.note: In 2025.12.5 the compass bus-type names are shifted: SLAVE now selects a bus with no compass support, and GYROAUTO selects the compass on the gyro's own bus (what SLAVE used to mean). So your value was not carried over, and your board's default applies. After flashing, check that your compass is detected; if it is connected through the gyro and isn't found, `set mag_bustype = GYROAUTO` selects that bus in 2025.12.5.

upgrade:mag-declination-signed-range.detail: PR #14019 changed the field from unsigned to signed and the range from 0..3599 to -300..300. PR #14206 confirmed the signed range.
upgrade:mag-declination-signed-range.note: Declination is still set in tenths of a degree, but west declinations are now stored as negative numbers, so a wrapped value like 3550 becomes -50. The new range is -300 to 300 (±30.0°). If your declination was larger than that, it was capped at the limit and your heading will be slightly off.

upgrade:min-throttle-folded-into-motor-i.detail: PR #13936 removed min_throttle. Analog idle output is now min_command + motor_idle/10, where it used to be min_throttle.
upgrade:min-throttle-folded-into-motor-i.note: On analog protocols (PWM, OneShot, Multishot, brushed), motor_idle now sets the idle level, as an offset above min_command. The converter worked out motor_idle from your min_throttle and min_command so idle stays the same. On DShot, min_throttle had no effect, and motor_idle takes your dshot_idle_value instead.

upgrade:motor-idle-protocol-aware.detail: PR #13936 renamed dshot_idle_value to motor_idle and merged min_throttle into it. Analog idle output is now min_command + motor_idle × 0.1.
upgrade:motor-idle-protocol-aware.note: On DShot or ProShot, motor_idle is your old dshot_idle_value, unchanged. On other protocols it is calculated as (min_throttle - min_command) × 10, limited to 0-2000, which gives the same idle output as before. Nothing to do unless your old values were outside that range.

upgrade:osd-canvas-size-hidden-behind-de.detail: PR #13595 removed canvas configuration from the CLI by putting these settings behind the OSD_CANVAS_SIZE_DEBUG build option, so normal builds of 2025.12.5 don't accept them. The PR intends restores of old configs not to override the canvas.
upgrade:osd-canvas-size-hidden-behind-de.note: Your old canvas size values are not carried over, and there is nothing to set again. The OSD canvas size now comes from the display (analog or digital FPV system) or the board's build defaults.

upgrade:pinio-box-dead-mode-ids-cleared.detail: PR #13816 gave permanent ID 3 to ALTHOLD and PR #13975 gave ID 11 to POS HOLD. Both IDs were unused in 4.5.5.
upgrade:pinio-box-dead-mode-ids-cleared.note: Any PINIO entry set to mode ID 3 or 11 never switched in 4.5.5, because those IDs had no mode. In 2025.12.5 they mean ALTHOLD and POS HOLD, so those entries are set to 255 (none) to keep the pin inactive. All other entries carry over unchanged.

upgrade:rescue-hover-throttle-moved.detail: PR #13816 moved the GPS Rescue hover throttle into a shared hover throttle setting, and PR #14136 renamed that setting to ap_hover_throttle.
upgrade:rescue-hover-throttle-moved.note: GPS Rescue now takes its hover throttle from ap_hover_throttle, a setting it shares with the other autopilot modes. Your value carried over in the same units. The new setting only accepts 1100-1700, so values outside that range were clamped to the nearest limit.

upgrade:rescue-throttle-max-moved.detail: PR #13954 moved GPS Rescue onto the shared altitude controller's throttle limits, and PR #14136 named the maximum ap_throttle_max.
upgrade:rescue-throttle-max-moved.note: GPS Rescue now takes its maximum throttle from ap_throttle_max, a limit shared by the autopilot modes. Your value carried over in the same units. The new setting only accepts 1400-2000, so a value below 1400 was raised to 1400.

upgrade:rescue-throttle-min-moved.detail: PR #13954 moved GPS Rescue onto the shared altitude controller's throttle limits, and PR #14136 named the minimum ap_throttle_min.
upgrade:rescue-throttle-min-moved.note: GPS Rescue now takes its minimum throttle from ap_throttle_min, a limit shared by the autopilot modes. Your value carried over in the same units. The new setting only accepts 1050-1400, so values outside that range were clamped to the nearest limit.

upgrade:rx-msp-feature-removed.detail: PR #13494 reworked how features are handled in the CLI. In 2025.12.x the RX_MSP feature still exists in the firmware, but the CLI cannot name it.
upgrade:rx-msp-feature-removed.note: The 2025.12.5 CLI has no way to name this feature, so your board will use its default setting for it. If you need MSP receiver input, turn it on in the Betaflight Configurator App after flashing.

upgrade:serial-port-ids-renamed.detail: PR #13585 and PR #14094 renumbered the internal serial port identifiers, and 2025.12.5 shows ports by name in the CLI. The old numbers are mapped one-to-one onto the new names.
upgrade:serial-port-ids-renamed.note: Serial port numbers are rewritten as port names (for example 0 becomes UART1 and 20 becomes VCP), the way 2025.12.5 writes them itself. The port functions and baud rates stay the same, so you don't need to do anything.

upgrade:thr-hover-from-old-thr-mid.detail: PR #14229 split the old thr_mid, which set both the stick position and the throttle output at the curve's midpoint, into thr_mid (stick position) and the new thr_hover (output).
upgrade:thr-hover-from-old-thr-mid.note: Your throttle curve stays the same. thr_hover now sets the throttle output at the curve's midpoint, and it is given your old thr_mid value, so the curve still runs through the same point. No action is needed unless you want to tune hover throttle separately.

upgrade:thr-mid-kept-as-stick-point.detail: PR #14229 made thr_mid only the stick position (x) of the curve midpoint and added thr_hover for the output (y); PR #14356 still builds the curve through those two values.
upgrade:thr-mid-kept-as-stick-point.note: Your value carries over and still sets the stick position of the throttle curve's midpoint. thr_hover is set to the same value, so your throttle curve is unchanged and no action is needed.
